slides: Welcome back, and now the cumulative graph. Cumulative means adding up.
In this graph, each point is not its own value. It's the sum of everything up to it.

slides.say: This graph shows the cumulative income of a company, Pixeltech, in the first half of two thousand thirteen.

slides: Across the bottom, the months. Going up, the cumulative income, in thousands of shekels. So eighty means eighty thousand shekels.

slides.say: The example says, Pixeltech's income in May was twenty thousand shekels.
Let's check. We go to May, and up to the line. We get to seventy. Seventy, not twenty. Why?
Because it's cumulative. Each point is the sum of everything up to it.
So the seventy at May is all the income from January to May together.
And the fifty at April is all the income up to April.
How much came in May alone? What was added from April to May. Seventy minus fifty is twenty. That's the twenty of the example.
Let's try March. At March it's fifty, and at February it's twenty. Fifty minus twenty is thirty. So thirty thousand came in March.
So one month is this point, minus the point before it.
Think of a bank account that we only put money into. It started at zero.
In January we put in ten thousand. The balance is ten.
In February we put in ten more. The balance is twenty.
In March, thirty more. The balance is fifty.
In April we put in nothing. The balance stays fifty.
And in May, twenty more. The balance is seventy. The graph shows the balance, not what we put in each month.
Here's a sample question. In which month did Pixeltech have no income at all?
We can see it straight away. From March to April the line is flat.
Flat means nothing was added. Up to March, fifty. Up to April, also fifty. Fifty minus fifty is zero.
So in April there was no income. The answer is April.
One more question. What was the total income in all the months?

slides: Do we add January, February, March, and so on? No. The graph already adds them up.

slides.say: The last point is the total. At June it's eighty, so eighty thousand shekels.
at: The last point is the total

slides.say: Careful, eighty is not the income in June. It's everything up to June.
The cumulative graph is not very common. But it's better to meet it here than for the first time on the exam.
